paper.title_en: Finite-Key Analysis for Multiple-Antenna Quantum Key Distribution with Continuous Variables
paper.abstract_en: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques, known for their use in wireless communications, can also find applications in quantum communications systems. This is, for instance, relevant to satellite-based quantum communications when atmospheric turbulence and the time-varying nature of the channel can make their implementation difficult. Here, we study the application of MIMO techniques to continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) in the realistic setting where a finite number of signals are exchanged. We show how data collected during the brief overpass time of low-earth-orbit satellites over ground stations can be processed to estimate MIMO channel parameters, extract a secret key, and quantify the key generation rate. For $2\times 2$ MIMO settings with Gaussian encoding and heterodyne detection, our finite-key analysis indicates that MIMO CV-QKD could outperform both multiplexed (with a nominal 3~dB improvement) and single-mode (with a nominal 6~dB nominal improvement) scenarios. Furthermore, we conjecture that the ultimate enhancement of a multiple-antenna CV-QKD system can be characterized by the product of the number of its inputs and outputs.
